Subject. Rice Shop Owners' Guild - receives instructional order purporting
to have emanated from local Kuomintang Headquarters.
Made by. C.D.I. Sih Tse Ling. Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford

At 9 a.m. March 20, 1940, the Shanghai
Municipality Rice Shop Owners' Guild, Lane 153,
52 Shanhaikwan Road, received a copy of an order
purporting to have emanated from the Shanghai
Municipality Kuomintang Headquarters of the
Chinese Kuomintang (Chungking) (上海特別市黨部).
This order instructed the Guild and its members
to clarify their attitude, through the medium
of press, towards the article in support of Wang
Ching Wei's peace movement, which appeared in
the Central China Daily News on March 17, 1940
and which purported to have originated from
some 100 local organizations headed by the
Shanghai Municipality Curios Dealers' Guild.
The despatch was delivered by hand to the
above guild by an unknown person. A copy of
the order together with translation is attached
hereto.
The person Wu Zao Zu (吳紹澍), who
signs the order as Chief of the Executive Committee
of the Shanghai Municipality Kuomintang
Headquarters of the Chinese Kuomintang is aged
about 37 and a native of Sungkiang. He graduated
from the Futan University at Shanghai, and formerly
served as a secretary in the Chung Shing Coal
Mining Company, Tai-er-chwang, Shantung. Prior

TRANSLATION

Order No. 54 of the Shanghai Municipality Headquarters
of the Chinese Kuomintang

On March 17, 1940, the Central China Daily News,
a puppet-administered newspaper, published a joint
telegram in the name of some 100 organizations headed
by the Shanghai Municipality Curios Dealers' Guild
(上海市古玩業同業公會), pledging support to the traitor
Wang's peace movement. The contents of the telegram
is absurd and it is thought that it may have been the
work of some persons who have illegally made use of
the names of these bodies to mislead the general public.
It is, therefore, requested that the organizations in
question publish in the Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao or
Chinese American Daily News, a denial or a statement
within four days of receipt of this order in order to
clarify their attitude. Failure to do so will result
in the suspension of these organizations and the
responsible persons concerned dealt with accordingly.

Signed: Wu Zhao Sz (吳兆滋), Chief.

中国国民党上海特别市党部第54号令

1940年3月17日，伪政权报纸《华中日报》以包括上海市古玩业同业公会（上海市古玩業同業公會）在内的约100个组织的名义发表联合通电，誓言支持汉奸汪精卫的和平运动。通电内容荒谬，被认为可能是某些人非法利用这些团体的名义来误导公众的行为。因此，要求有关组织在收到本命令后四天内，在《新闻报》、《申报》或《中美日报》上刊登否认声明或澄清态度的声明。若不照办，将导致这些组织被停办，相关责任人将受到相应处理。

签署人：吴兆滋（吳兆滋），主任。
盖章：中国国民党上海特别市党部执行委员会。

SUMMARIZED TRANSLATION

Gentlemen:
        We are very pleased to see that you
have not wavered even though unscrupulous means
have been employed by traitor Wang to induce you
to fall into his trap. Your attitude reflects
righteousness which still prevails. Recently,
however, it was learned that traitor Wang and his
followers, had engaged themselves energetically
in preparing the establishment of a puppet regime.
They have made certain pro-Wang documents which
are false and have coerced various trade associations
to chop them. It is further learned that in the
event of the puppet regime becoming established,
they will resort to other contemptible means to
make local trade circles hoist their flag in
celebration. We hope, that you will adopt the
same attitude you have displayed in the past in
pointing out to your fellow-traders how they should
be loyal to the National Government - first and last.
Should there be certain weak-minded individuals,
you must explain to them the importance of
"righteousness" in order to confirm their belief.

Shanghai Municipality Kuomintang
Headquarters
Chief Woo Chao Sz (吳紹澍)
(chopped)
March 16, the 29th year
of the Chinese Republic.

诸位先生：

中国国民党上海特别市党部
主任 吴绍澍（吳紹澍）

Made by D.I. Pan Lien-chih Forwarded by C Crawford D.I.

Following the withdrawal of the Chinese troops from the
Shanghai area in November, 1937, the majority of the 120
officers of the local Kuomintang left Shanghai for Hankow
or for other services with the forces at the front, leaving
about twenty members behind in charge of Mr. Mo Yung (毛雲).
Because of the unfavourable circumstances prevailing at
present in Shanghai, these twenty persons have remained
inactive, living apart from one another and taking no part
in the Tangpu activities.

Of those twenty members, the following are understood
to be still in Shanghai :-

Mr. Mo Yung ( 毛雲 ), a lawyer by profession and
at present engaged in refugee relief work sponsored
by the Refugee Relief Committee of the Pootung
Fellow Countrymen's Association, 1454 Avenue
Edward VII.

Mr. Yue Yao-chiu ( 余耀球), former executive member
of the Investigation Department of the Tangpu, and
at present engaged in relief work conducted by the
Taichong, Kading and Paosan Fellow Countrymen's
Relief Association, 12 Rue du Consulat.

Mr. Chun Pai-yung ( 龔沛雲 ), former executive member
of the People's Movement Department of the Tangpu
and also former committee member of the General
Labour Union, and at present in charge of the
Repatriation Department of the Refugee Relief
Committee of the Pootung Fellow Countrymen's
Association, 1454 Avenue Edward VII.

MAINICHI

CHIANG KAI SHEK DECIDES ON REMOVAL OF DISTRICT
KUOMINTANG FROM SHANGHAI

It has been frequently
reported to the effect that a number of foreign residents
as well as the Chinese in Shanghai would like to have
the District Kuomintang, the Blue Shirts Society, the
C. C. Corps and all other anti-Japanese organizations
removed from Shanghai in order to prevent a recurrence
of such incidents like the case of lese majeste
committed by the "New Life Weekly".
According to information
received from reliable Chinese sources, Chiang Kai
Shek has decided to remove the District Kuomintang,
which is strongly anti-Japanese, from Shanghai because
he has come to the conclusion that the presence of the
District Kuomintang in Shanghai may give rise to further
trouble between Japan and China and injure the prestige
of the Kuomintang and the Central Government among
foreigners. Chiang Kai Shek will so arrange matters
that the withdrawal will appear to be in accordance
with the wishes of the Chinese people and not have the
appearance of a surrender to Japan's wishes.
Chiang Kai Shek first sought the
understanding of local Chinese circles regarding the
removal. A few days ago, the Chinese District
Federation, the Chamber of Commerce and other public
bodies sent a joint letter to Chiang Kai Shek asking
for the removal of the District Kuomintang from Shanghai.
It is not known when and in what manner the petition
will be acted upon.
Well-informed Chinese and
foreigners in Shanghai generally believe that the
withdrawal of the Kuomintang from Shanghai is not
intended as a gesture for the promotion of Sino-Japanese
relations but rather as a measure to prevent further
trouble between Japan and China because in the event
of further trouble arising the power of the Central
Government would be destroyed. For this reason ,
the withdrawal is not regarded as a pacification measure
but rather for the purpose of strengthening the
activities of the Blue Shirts Society which is Chiang
Kai Shek's most powerful political organization. Chiang
Kai Shek was endeavour to convert the Kuomintang
into a private and secret organization like the Blue
Shirts Society.

THE PUBLICATION OF THE "NEW LIFE WEEKLY"

a petition with the 2nd Branch of the Kiangsu High Court
pointing out that although the Court has issued an order
prohibiting the distribution of the "New Life Weekly"
no order prohibiting its publication has been issued .
For this reason the petition requests the Court to issue
an order prohibiting the publication of the weekly in
question in accordance with Section 2 of Article 41 of
the Chinese Press Law.
The Court will hold a conference
to-day to consider the petition.

蒋介石决定将区国民党党部撤出上海

此前屡有报道指出，在上海的外国居民以及中国人希望将区国民党党部、蓝衣社、CC系及其他所有反日组织撤出上海，以防止类似《新生周刊》犯下的“大不敬”案这样的事件再次发生。
据可靠中方消息来源获悉，蒋介石已决定将强烈反日的区国民党党部撤出上海，因为他得出结论认为，区国民党党部留在上海可能会引起中日之间进一步的麻烦，并损害国民党及中央政府在外人中的威望。蒋介石将对此事做出安排，使撤退看起来符合中国人的意愿，而不显得是对日本意愿的屈服。
蒋介石首先就撤出事宜寻求当地华人圈子的理解。几天前，华界联合会、商会及其他公共团体联名致信蒋介石，要求将区国民党党部撤出上海。尚不知该请愿将在何时以何种方式得到处理。
上海消息灵通的中外人士普遍认为，国民党撤出上海并非为了促进中日关系的一种姿态，而是为了防止中日之间发生进一步麻烦的措施，因为如果发生进一步的麻烦，中央政府的权力将被摧毁。因此，此次撤退不被视为一种安抚措施，而是为了加强作为蒋介石最强大政治组织的蓝衣社的活动。蒋介石正努力将国民党转变为像蓝衣社那样的私人秘密组织。

市政检察官请求中国法院取缔《新生周刊》的出版

7月18日，工部局向江苏高等法院第二分院提交请愿书，指出虽然法院已发布命令禁止分发《新生周刊》，但并未发布禁止其出版的命令。因此，该请愿书请求法院根据《中华民国出版法》第四十一条第二款的规定，发布命令禁止该周刊的出版。
法院将于今日召开会议审议该请愿书。

Kuomintang organ in Shanghai, and its duties, apart from
directing party affairs and endeavouring to imbue the people

the work of the administrative organs, with the object of
bringing to the notice of the National Government through

independent of the Shanghai Municipality, the local
administrative organ in the Chinese controlled territory,
but they cooperate in anything in which they are mutually

The local Kuomintang directs and supervises the
organization of labour unions. Any body of workers
intending to organize a union must first apply to the local
Kuomintang for permission and when permission has been
granted, a representative of the Kuomintang will supervise
and direct the preparation, after which the union has to
apply to the Bureau of Social Affairs for registration.

It is generally considered that any movement,
either political or labour, should be conducted under the
supervision and direction of the local Kuomintang and that that
which has been sponsored without the knowledge of this organ
is regarded as illegal and liable to be suppressed. Being
an organ for the party affairs, it has, however, no
administrative or executive power. Apart from the fact
that it is authorized to instruct any union to cease functioning
pending reorganization or otherwise, any decision which the
Kuomintang has formed has to be executed by the local Chinese

At present it ostensibly exercises control over
local labour unions more or less through the General Labour
Union, as the majority of the members of the General Labour
Union, such as Chu Hsueh-fan (朱学范 ) are supporters of

them is far from being strong and the reluctant obedience
of workers to the instructions of the Kuomintang as well as

fact that the workers dare not raise much opposition against
the Authority in order to avoid the accusation of being
reactionaries.

education and film censorship, the local Kuomintang keeps
constant surveillance and conducts investigation into any
